outcome: use of general anesthesia for Cesarean delivery
cohort: 320 pregnant women (160 with antepartum thrombocytopenia and 160 non-thrombocytopenic controls), matched for age, parity, and gestational age, from a tertiary care center.
finding: Antepartum thrombocytopenia is associated with a higher likelihood of operative delivery, increased reliance on general anesthesia, and a higher incidence of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: The Cesarean section rate was significantly higher in the thrombocytopenic group (48.1% vs. 29.4%).
gest_age: Gestational age was used as a matching criterion for participants.
